input_hashes.d_form_note: D-isoascorbic acid / erythorbate; similar potency (1316 uM, 300%) per PI; stereo undefined in source
pi_domain_notes: Reference: L-ascorbic acid (compound 1; potency 1797 uM, 286% potentiation) is the reference PAM for this series.
D-form probe: compound 2 (D-isoascorbic acid / erythorbate) has similar potency (1316 uM, 300%); PI-note L/D assignment - raw stereo undefined (stereo_has_undefined_stereo=True).
High potency arm: 3-O-substituted ascorbate (PI shorthand '3-O-ethyl'). Best-annotated instance: compound 12, 3-O-propargyl-5,6-acetonide, 0.198 uM - no literal O-ethyl analog in the dataset.
Second high potency active: 6-bromo-6-deoxy ascorbate (compound 25, 2.63 uM).
All other validated actives are >1 mM (compounds 3/18/24: 6077/1288/1202 uM), i.e. substantially less potent than compounds 12 and 25.
Selectivity (PI note): ascorbic acid is a selective potentiator of alpha9alpha10. NOT modeled - no cross-subunit selectivity data in the repository.

PI stereoelectronic SAR hypotheses (recorded verbatim from PI; NOT all verifiable from the 30-compound set; see honesty flags): (a) enolic hydroxyls required for potentiation - PARTIAL support: 2,3-bis-O-alkylation ablates activity (0/6) but mono-etherification is tolerated (2-O compound 24 active; 3-O compound 12 active/most potent), so a free enol OH per se is not required; (b) C2=C3 olefin essential - UNTESTED: no saturation probe exists in the 30-compound set; (c) C-3 etherification increases potency - supported ONLY for compound 12 (3-O-propargyl-5,6-acetonide, 0.198 uM); 7/8 3-O-alkoxy acetonide analogs (compounds 5-11) and all open-chain 3-O-alkoxy (compounds 19-21) are inactive, so 'alkyl well tolerated' overstates the SAR; (d) C-6 substitution decreases potency - NOT SUPPORTED: 6-bromo-6-deoxy (compound 25) is 2.63 uM (~680x gain over reference) and 6-O-benzyl (compound 18, 1288 uM) is comparable to the reference; no C-6 substitution in the dataset reduces potency.

Ryanodine analogy (PI hypothesis, SPECULATIVE): ascorbic acid shares structural and functional similarities with the polyhydroxy cyclic moieties of ryanodine; proposed metal ion-dipole/chelation and hydrogen-bonding roles for the enediol. Not testable from the current dataset; framing only.

Planned synthetic probes (PENDING_SYNTHESIS, NOT executable now; no fabricated molecules): Study 1.4 (C-5/C-6 role) - fully deoxygenated analog 4.1 via Barton-McCombie deoxygenation (C-3 Mitsunobu protection; C-5/C-6 di-imidazole thiocarbonate activation; radical removal of both oxygens); a SEPARATE dehydration/elimination route (deoxygenation does NOT create an alkene) to a rigid C-5/C-6 olefinic handle for Ru-catalyzed cross-metathesis, yielding olefinated analogs 4.3 with varied R5 groups to probe steric/electronic effects; ~10 analogs planned; 4.1 and 4.3 serve as platforms for C-2/C-3 modification. Hypothesis: 4.1 reduced potentiation (compound-specific - ID3 acetonide 6077 uM is ~3.4x weaker than reference, but 6-Br is a counter-example), select rigid 4.3 may retain or enhance activity.

Planned synthetic probes (PENDING_SYNTHESIS): Study 1.5 (aza/lactam-constrained ascorbate mimics) - L-serine-derived chiral amino-butenolide (Dutta lactone) intermediate affords azacarbohydrates 5.2 via intramolecular cyclization; the unsaturated lactone is then converted to bicyclic lactones via Pd-catalyzed cyclopropanation (5.3a), in-situ peroxy epoxidation (5.3b), or in-situ N-mediated aziridination (5.3c); ~8 analogs planned per category; scaffolds differ from ascorbate in stereoelectronics (oxygen replaced/modulated by CH2 or N).
